correctness.rationale: On the mean-zero subspace, L≥λ₂P. A positive semidefinite Q vanishing on constants and with edge squared distances (1,s²,1) therefore gives λ₂≤B/tr Q for all individual allocations. In the line regime the centered positions (0,1,1+s,2+s) give this Q as xxᵀ; the leaf equations and one hub equation give the stated conductances and Lx=(B/C_line)x. In the split regime x has positions (−h,0,s,s+1), with ph=q+(q+1)s; the correction p(1−h²)/(p−1) times the left-contrast projector makes every left spoke's Q-distance squared one. It raises tr Q from ph²+s²+q(1+s)² to C_split. The proposed split weights solve Lx=(B/C_split)x and have budget B by p+q(1+s)+s²(1+q+q/s)=C_split. An independent quotient inertia check confirms both gaps: write λ=B/C, decompose into left and right contrasts and the class-constant block, and study the latter after subtracting λI. For s>s_c both leaf pivots are positive. The remaining two-hub Schur complement has a zero direction from x and a negative eigenvalue in its inertia because constants give a negative direction in the quotient. When s≤s_c, b>λ and a=λ. After eliminating the positive right leaf pivot, the left average and U form an invertible two-by-two pivot of negative determinant −pa². The final scalar is zero because x is an eigenvector. Thus there is one quotient eigenvalue below λ and one at λ in both cases, with p−1 additional left contrasts at λ exactly when a=λ. All candidates are positive. Equality of the trace forces (L−λP)Q=0, so Lx=λx; all individual leaf rates and then the bridge are forced by the nonzero jumps. Finally, measuring the positions from 1 gives squared sum C_split; centering them at their mean μ subtracts N(μ−1)², giving the claimed denominator identity. At the positive threshold the weights match with μ=1, the gap is C¹, and its right minus left second derivative is 2B(q+1)²/(NC²)>0 at the common denominator C. For p=q only the strict line regime occurs.
residual_risks: Only positive prices, positive budgets and continuous-time Laplacian gaps are covered. The numerical output is corroborative and does not attest arbitrary real prices or general graphs.

evidence: Weighted-cost SDP covers the optimization as an instance and arbitrary lengths are admitted in the embedding dual. The explicit tree theorem in Wappler uses equal edge lengths; the Richter–Rocha double-broom theorem also uses uniform price, as does the Fiedler definition quoted in the sources inspected.
